messages:
matt: Quick proposal: roll out dynamic JSON log redaction + region-aware sampling for GPU telemetry to cut ingest cost and reduce PII risk. Short TL;DR: add pii_level + consent flag to envelopes, apply hashing for high-sensitivity fields when consent=false, and use per-region sampling policies tied to load. Canary and alert tuning required.

matt: Example envelope we want to standardize (small change to current schema):
```
{
  "ts": 1742100000,
  "service": "gpu-agent",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "pii_level": "low|medium|high",
  "consent": false,
  "payload": { ... },
  "sensitive_fields_hashed": ["user_email_hash", "request_body_hash"]
}
```

anya: 👍 overall seems sane. quick q: how do existing dashboards distinguish hashed vs original field? parsers will need to know field suffix convention.

matt: we'll add a compatibility layer in ingest that maps hashed fields to canonical names with a metadata flag so dashboards still read canonical keys but values will be masked. intent is to avoid schema drift.

raj: will this break any alerting rules that look for specific string matches (eg model-version tags inside request_body)? we use regex in a couple of alerts.

anya: good point. we should add an allowlist of regex-extractable fields preserved un-hashed for monitoring only (not raw PII).

sophia: oncall concern: sampling changes + redaction could hide signals for brief flapping. we should adjust alert windows. suggest: increase evaluation window for the 95th latency alert from 3m->10m during canary.

oncall-bot: FYI: current oncall schedule for eng-runtime is @marcus this week.

marcus: I can own the canary. propose canary cluster: gpu-ingest-canary-2 (us-west-2) for 48h. will monitor: ingest_size_bytes, dropped_fields_total, parse_errors_total, avg_token_per_payload.

matt: planned sampling defaults per region (canary):
- us-west-2: telemetry: 10% -> 2% for token-heavy messages
- eu-central-1: telemetry: 8% -> 1% (consent=false)
- ap-southeast-1: telemetry: 5% -> 1%
We will allow overrides via LOG_SAMPLING_POLICY config per cluster.

sophia: Prometheus tune suggestion for alerts to reduce noise:
- use rate(parse_errors_total[5m]) > 0.1 for 5m instead of instant
- for latency SLO breaches use: increase_over_baseline = (histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(req_duration_bucket[10m])) - baseline) > 200ms

matt: example PromQL for parse-error alert:
```
sum by(cluster) (rate(parse_errors_total{job="ingest"}[5m])) > 0.2
```
And wrap it with `for 10m` in the rule to avoid one-off spikes.

compliance-bot: Note: EU logs must not send direct PII to third-party indexers. any hashed/pseudonymized field must be irreversible. store mapping only if customer explicitly requests and signs DPA addendum. Add audit log entry for any mapping creation.

anya: I'll add parser compatibility unit tests and a transform test that verifies hashed fields are irreversible.

raj: downstream ETL: suggest a non-breaking transform step in ingest-lambda that emits both legacy keys and new envelope metadata for 30 days, then cut legacy after verified.

matt: rollout plan (high level):
1) PR with ingest transform + LOG_SAMPLING_POLICY feature flag (INF-3242) -> staging tests.
2) Canary on gpu-ingest-canary-2 (us-west-2) for 48h monitoring metrics above.
3) Gradual region rollouts with telemetry-based adjustments.
4) Remove legacy keys after 30d stable.

matt: Grafana dashboards to update:
- ingest overview: add panel for sensitive_fields_hashed rate
- cost dashboard: tokens_ingested_by_region -> show before/after sampling delta
- SLO dashboard: add canary state annotation when feature flag enabled

marcus: I'll spin up canary tomorrow at 06:00 UTC and post the runbook checkin.

matt: created INF-3242 and draft PR: https://git.redwood/infraproj/ingest/merge_requests/12 (please review).

anya: I'll own parser tests and a changelog entry for docs.

sophia: I'll adjust alerting rules and push a Grafana tempboard for the canary.

raj: I'll coordinate with ETL folks to add the 30d compatibility window.

compliance-bot: Reminder: include a short audit playbook in the PR describing how to revert and how to demonstrate policy compliance to customers.

matt: nice. if no blockers I'll merge the feature flag PR after tests pass and schedule the canary. ping me for any cross-team dependencies. :thumbsup:

marcus: noted. posting canary runbook link in a sec.

matt: thanks all.
